categories.title: EC-405 Theory
categories.description: Language rules, gate and dataflow modelling, behavioural blocks and the design flow behind the first three EC-405 units.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a hardware description language such as Verilog?
options: To describe digital hardware so it can be simulated and, for a synthesizable subset, implemented in hardware
To style web pages and control browser layouts
To replace the operating system on a personal computer
To measure analogue voltages with a multimeter
questions.explanation: Verilog describes the structure and behaviour of digital circuits. Simulation checks the description, and synthesis tools can map a synthesizable subset onto real hardware.

questions.prompt: Which declaration creates a single-bit net that is suitable for a continuous `assign` statement?
questions.explanation: `wire` declares a net driven continuously by a primitive, an instance output or an `assign`. A `reg` is assigned procedurally inside an `always` or `initial` block.

questions.prompt: What does this complete program print?
questions.explanation: Bitwise AND gives 1 only when both bits are 1. Here one input is 0, so `y` is 0 and `$display` prints `0`.

questions.prompt: Which gate has this truth table?
questions.explanation: The output is 1 when the inputs differ and 0 when they match. That is exclusive-OR, written `a ^ b` in Verilog.

questions.prompt: Which Verilog expression means “`a` AND NOT `b`”?
questions.explanation: `&` is bitwise AND and `~` is bitwise NOT, so `a & ~b` is high only when `a` is 1 and `b` is 0.

questions.prompt: What is the value of `y` after this assignment?
questions.explanation: AND is applied bit by bit: 1010 & 1100 = 1000. The leftmost bit is 1 only because both operands have a 1 there.

questions.prompt: Why will this module fail to compile?
options: The `assign` statement is missing its terminating semicolon
`input wire a` is not legal Verilog
questions.explanation: Every assignment statement ends with a semicolon. The missing `;` after `assign y = a` is a syntax error, so compilation stops before simulation.

questions.prompt: Which construct is a continuous assignment?
questions.explanation: `assign` creates a continuous dataflow assignment. It re-evaluates whenever a signal on the right-hand side changes, without waiting for a clock or an initial block.

questions.prompt: In the gate primitive `and g1(y, a, b);`, which signal is the output?
questions.explanation: A gate primitive lists the output first, followed by its inputs. Here `y` is the output and `a`, `b` are the inputs; `g1` is the instance name.

questions.prompt: Why are nonblocking assignments (`<=`) normally used in an edge-triggered `always` block?
options: They schedule updates at the end of the time step, which models several flip-flops updating together
They execute faster than any other assignment
They automatically add a clock divider
They prevent the block from being simulated
questions.explanation: Nonblocking assignments evaluate their right-hand sides first and update at the end of the time step. This avoids order-dependent cascades and models synchronous registers correctly.

questions.prompt: After this combinational block runs, what is `y`?
questions.explanation: Blocking assignments execute in order. The first statement assigns `a`, then the second overwrites it with `b`, so the final value is `b`.

questions.prompt: Why is a testbench normally not synthesized into hardware?
options: It generates stimulus and checks outputs; it is simulation-only code, not a hardware description
It contains too many comments for a synthesizer
questions.explanation: A testbench drives the design, observes results and reports pass or fail. It has no physical input/output ports and is not intended to become a circuit.

categories.title: EC-410 Laboratory
categories.description: Gates, adders, subtractors, a four-bit parallel adder, multiplexers and demultiplexers — the six experiments in the current laboratory.

questions.prompt: Which gate produces a 1 only when both of its inputs are 1?
questions.explanation: The AND gate is the product term: `y = a & b`. Its output is 1 for the single input combination 11 and 0 for the other three rows.

questions.prompt: Which pair of expressions describes the sum and carry of a half adder?
questions.explanation: The sum bit is 1 when exactly one input is 1, which is XOR. The carry is 1 only when both inputs are 1, which is AND.

questions.prompt: This table shows the carry output of a full adder. Which expression matches it?
questions.explanation: The carry is the majority function: it is 1 when at least two of the three inputs are 1. The three product terms cover every such pair.

questions.prompt: In a four-bit ripple-carry adder, what does the final carry-out indicate?
options: The unsigned sum needed a fifth bit because it exceeded 15
questions.explanation: Four sum bits represent 0–15. A final carry of 1 means the true sum is 16 or more, so the unsigned result has overflowed the four-bit field.

questions.prompt: How many select lines does a 4:1 multiplexer require?
questions.explanation: Four data inputs need four distinct addresses, and two select bits provide 2² = 4 combinations: 00, 01, 10 and 11.

questions.prompt: How many outputs does a 1:4 demultiplexer have, and how many are high at once?
questions.explanation: A 1:4 demultiplexer routes one data input to one of four outputs. The selected output follows the data input; the other three remain low.

questions.prompt: How many select lines does an 8:1 multiplexer require?
questions.explanation: Three select bits give 2³ = 8 addresses, enough to choose one of the eight data inputs.

questions.prompt: What is the five-bit value of `s`?
questions.explanation: 0110 is 6 and 0011 is 3, so the sum is 9. In five bits, 9 is `01001`; the extra bit preserves the carry.

questions.prompt: The design declares an output named `cout`, but the testbench uses this instance. What is wrong?
options: The named port `.carry` does not exist in the design; it should be `.cout`
Named port connections are illegal in Verilog-2001
A testbench cannot instantiate a module
questions.explanation: Named connections must match the design’s port names exactly. A misspelled or nonexistent port is an elaboration error, even though the syntax looks valid.

questions.prompt: Why does a self-checking testbench print a PASS or FAIL summary?
options: It compares observed outputs with expected values so the result is visible without manual waveform inspection
It makes the simulation run faster
It replaces the need for a design module
questions.explanation: The testbench applies known inputs, checks the outputs and counts mismatches. A final `PASS: n/n` line gives a clear, repeatable result for the experiment.

questions.prompt: For a half subtractor, what are the difference and borrow when `a = 0` and `b = 1`?
questions.explanation: 0 − 1 cannot be done in one bit without borrowing. The difference is 1 and a borrow of 1 is taken from the next column, matching `D = a ^ b` and `Bout = ~a & b`.

questions.prompt: A 1:8 demultiplexer has `Din = 1` and select `101`. Which output is high?
questions.explanation: The select value 101 is binary 5, so output Y5 is selected. It follows the data input and becomes 1; all other outputs remain 0.

categories.title: Circuit Lab
categories.description: Ideal logic levels, Boolean identities, routing blocks and the clocked D flip-flop from the interactive demonstrations.

questions.prompt: When is the output of a two-input NAND gate equal to 0?
questions.explanation: NAND is NOT-AND. The AND term is 1 only for 11, so the NAND output is 0 only for that row and 1 for the other three.

questions.prompt: What condition makes the output of an XOR gate equal to 1?
options: The first input is 1 and the second is 0 only
questions.explanation: XOR is the difference detector. It outputs 1 for 01 and 10, and 0 for 00 and 11.

questions.prompt: Which expression is the XNOR function?
questions.explanation: XNOR is the complement of XOR, so it is 1 when the inputs match. Verilog also provides the `~^` operator for this function.

questions.prompt: For a half subtractor, which input row produces a borrow output of 1?
questions.explanation: A borrow is needed only when subtracting 1 from 0. The borrow expression is `Bout = ~a & b`, which is 1 for the row 01.

questions.prompt: In a 2-to-4 decoder with an active-high enable, what happens when `EN = 0`?
options: All four outputs are forced low
All four outputs are forced high
Output Y0 is high and the others are low
questions.explanation: The enable gates every output. With `EN = 0`, no output can be selected, so all four outputs remain 0 regardless of the select inputs.

questions.prompt: In the 4-to-2 priority encoder, which request wins when several inputs are high?
options: The request that arrived first in time
All requests are encoded at once
questions.explanation: Priority runs from R3 down to R0. The highest active request determines the encoded output, and the valid output shows that at least one request is present.

questions.prompt: How many outputs of a 4-bit magnitude comparator are high at the same time?
options: Exactly one of GT, EQ or LT
questions.explanation: For any pair of unsigned four-bit values, exactly one relation holds: greater than, equal to, or less than. The comparator asserts the matching output only.

questions.prompt: The D flip-flop has an asynchronous active-high reset. If `RST = 1`, what is `Q` after the reset is applied?
options: `Q` waits for the next rising edge
questions.explanation: Asynchronous reset acts without waiting for a clock edge. Asserting `RST` clears the stored value, so `Q` becomes 0 and `Q̄` becomes 1.

questions.prompt: How many rows are needed for an exhaustive truth table of a 4:1 multiplexer with four data inputs and two select inputs?
questions.explanation: Six independent binary inputs (D0–D3 plus S1 and S0) produce 2⁶ = 64 combinations. The table must cover every select and data pattern.

questions.prompt: What function does `Y = (A & S) | (B & ~S)` implement?
options: A 2:1 multiplexer choosing between A and B
questions.explanation: When `S = 1`, the first term passes A and the second is 0. When `S = 0`, the second term passes B. That is a 2:1 multiplexer.

questions.prompt: Why does the Circuit Lab describe itself as a logic workbench rather than a timing simulator?
options: It evaluates ideal logic levels and does not model gate delays or analogue rise and fall times
It only works with analogue voltages
It compiles Verilog in the browser
It requires a physical FPGA connected by USB
questions.explanation: The lab shows the intended Boolean behaviour immediately. Real hardware has propagation delays, setup and hold requirements, and analogue effects that a gate-level truth-table model does not represent.

categories.title: Playground Fundamentals
categories.description: Compiling, running and reading a Verilog project on your own machine, plus the habits that keep a design and its testbench honest.

questions.prompt: Which command compiles `design.v` and `tb.v` into an Icarus simulation image?
questions.explanation: `iverilog` is the compiler. `-g2001` selects Verilog-2001, `-o` names the output image, and the two source files follow.

questions.prompt: Which command executes the compiled simulation image?
questions.explanation: `vvp` is the Icarus runtime. It executes the simulation image produced by `iverilog` and prints any `$display` or `$monitor` output.

questions.prompt: What does the `-g2001` option tell Icarus Verilog?
questions.explanation: `-g2001` selects the language standard. The examples use Verilog-2001 port declarations such as `input wire a`, so the same generation is used for verification.

questions.prompt: Which file in a Playground project is intended to become hardware?
questions.explanation: The design contains the synthesizable module. The testbench drives it for simulation, the transcript records the result, and `simulation.out` is the compiled simulation image.

questions.prompt: Both registers are four bits wide. What does this print?
questions.explanation: The expression is evaluated in a four-bit context here, so the carry out of the top bit is lost. 15 + 1 wraps to 0 and prints `0000`. A five-bit destination would preserve `10000`.

questions.prompt: The design file defines `module and2(...)`, but the testbench instantiates `and_gate uut (...);`. What will happen?
options: Elaboration fails because `and_gate` is not a known module
The testbench silently renames the design
The simulation runs but ignores the inputs
questions.explanation: A module instance must name a module that exists in the compiled source set. The mismatch produces an “Unknown module type” error before simulation starts.

questions.prompt: What is the role of `$finish` in a testbench?
questions.explanation: `$finish` stops the simulation and returns control to the runtime. Without it, a testbench with no more events may need an explicit end or may appear to hang.

questions.prompt: Why does the Playground stop calling an example “verified” after you edit either file?
options: The displayed transcript belongs to the original files and was not regenerated for your edit
The browser automatically deletes the example
Editing always introduces a syntax error
questions.explanation: The reference transcript is evidence for the exact shipped sources. Once the text changes, only a new local compile and run can show what your version does.

questions.prompt: Which browser key stores optional Playground drafts?
questions.explanation: Drafts use their own versioned key. `va.progress` stores lesson and experiment completion, `va.quizzes` stores quiz attempts, and `va.theme` stores the colour theme.

questions.prompt: After downloading `design.v` and `tb.v` from the Playground, what is the correct next step?
options: Open a terminal in that folder, compile both files with Icarus, run the image and compare the output
Open the files in a browser tab and wait for the page to compile them
Rename both files to `.txt` and submit them
Upload them to the Playground for automatic grading
questions.explanation: The Playground prepares the files; it does not compile them. The documented workflow is a local `iverilog` compile followed by `vvp`, with the transcript compared against your own result.

questions.prompt: Which declaration describes a single-bit output net in a Verilog-2001 module port list?
questions.explanation: `output wire y` declares a net driven out of the module. `output reg y` is procedural, `input wire y` is an input, and `wire output y` has the keywords in the wrong order.
